truths.truth: All six --dir seams refuse an empty and a trailing valueless --dir with one JSON line naming the flag, exit 1; an ABSENT --dir still resolves to the process cwd
truths.evidence: Ran all 12 arms in /code/cadence. Each of git-publish.mjs reap --dir '' --branch nosuchbranch-xyz / --dir (valueless), git-branch.mjs tags, release-bump.mjs bump --version 1.1.0, land-cleanup.mjs gate, worktree-base.mjs resolve, issue-check.mjs check answered exactly {"ok":false,"reason":"missing-flag-value","detail":"--dir"} at exit=1. Baseline reversed: git-branch.mjs tags --dir '' no longer prints the tag list. Regression control: git-branch.mjs tags with NO --dir still returns {"ok":true,"tags":["v1.0.0",...]} exit 0.

truths.truth: The full bin test suite passes with zero failures and lib/seam-input.mjs's header no longer claims two surviving --dir contracts
truths.evidence: node --test 'cadence-core/bin/*.test.mjs' -> tests 2321, pass 2321, fail 0, duration 17.5s (one full-suite run). cadence-core/bin/lib/seam-input.mjs:19-20 now reads 'THE TWO FLAG READERS ARE TWO CONTRACTS, AND BOTH ARE LIVE' about optionalFlag vs flagValue generally, and :41-45 states '`--dir` reads through flagValue at EVERY seam (phase 2 D-01), reversing this header's earlier guarantee that its five callers kept the permissive reader.' The old two-surviving---dir-contracts claim is gone.

truths.truth: release-bump bump --date refuses every malformed spelling under a new bad-date code at exit 1 leaving CHANGELOG.md byte-identical, while a well-formed --date still writes the dated heading
truths.evidence: In-place refusal arms (release-bump.mjs bump --version 1.1.0 --date X): not-a-date, 2026-13-45, 2026-8-1, '' and a trailing valueless --date each returned {"ok":false,"action":"refuse","reason":"bad-date","detail":"--date must be YYYY-MM-DD ..."} exit 1; the newline-carrying value ('2026-08-18\n## [9.9.9] - forged') returned the distinct detail '--date cannot contain a newline: ... a newline forges a second release section' exit 1. CHANGELOG.md sha256 1a96df56e76bda2bff04bab87b95cfe817b152fd6ebc9b3f96430f534a01320d identical before and after all six runs; git status clean. Accepted arm in a throwaway fixture (scratchpad/rbfix with .claude-plugin/plugin.json at 1.0.0): --version 1.1.0 --date 2026-08-18 returned ok:true action:bumped and the file now carries '## [1.1.0] - 2026-08-18'. Absent --date still dates today ('## [1.1.0] - 2026-08-19' in a second fixture).

truths.truth: A malformed --date refuses ahead of bump(), including against a directory with no plugin manifest where nothing would be written
truths.evidence: Empty throwaway dir: release-bump.mjs bump --dir <tmp> --version 1.1.0 --date not-a-date -> {"ok":false,"action":"refuse","reason":"bad-date",...} exit 1. Control on the same dir with no --date -> {"ok":true,"action":"skip","reason":"no-plugin-manifest",...} exit 0, so the refusal genuinely precedes the manifest read rather than the dir simply erroring.

truths.truth: A phase spelling that cannot round-trip is refused at seed-reqs and cursor set; 2 and 2.1 still succeed and phase-done --n 02 still checks its roadmap box
truths.evidence: In place (no writes, git status unchanged): planning.mjs seed-reqs --phase 1.10 -> {"ok":false,"reason":"bad-args","detail":"seed-reqs --phase \"1.10\" is written here as phase 1.1, a different phase - send --phase \"1.1\", or rename phases/1.10/ to phases/1.1/"}; cursor set --phase 1.10 the same with the cursor-set prefix; also 1.0 -> 'written here as phase 1' and 01 -> 'written here as phase 1'. Accepted arms in a copied fixture (scratchpad/fx/.planning): seed-reqs --phase 2 -> {"ok":true,"phase":2,...}; cursor set --phase 2 --status planned --next x -> ok:true; cursor set --phase 2.1 --status planned --next x --name Sub --total 5 -> {"ok":true,"cursor":{"phase":2.1,...}}; seed-reqs --phase 2.1 passes the spelling gate (fails later on no-plans, not bad-args). phase-done --n 02 -> {"ok":true,"roadmap":{"line":37,"now":"[x]"},...} and the fixture ROADMAP line 37 is now '[x]'.

truths.truth: The shared numeric readers (requireInt, requireCursorNumber, normalizeNumber, scanIssueRefs) refuse values outside the safe-integer range instead of rounding or yielding Infinity
truths.evidence: Direct calls: requireInt('9007199254740993') -> {"ok":false}, requireInt('1'+400 digits) -> {"ok":false}, requireInt('42') -> {ok:true,value:42}; requireCursorNumber same three results; scanIssueRefs('fixes #9007199254740993') -> [] and the 400-digit form -> [], while 'fixes #42' -> [42]. normalizeNumber is module-private (cadence-core/bin/lib/issue-decision.mjs:77, guarded by Number.isSafeInteger at :78 and :81); its behavior is pinned by the named test 'a number OUTSIDE the safe-integer range is unreadable, never a neighbour (ARG-04)' (issue-decision.test.mjs:343, exercising HOST_TABLE.forgejo.normalize). Ran by name: 5/5 pass (require-int.test.mjs safe-range tests for requireInt, requireCursorNumber, requirePhaseArg plus both issue-decision ARG-04 tests).

truths.truth: config.mjs reports Object.prototype members as unknown keys at every face, and does not fabricate a retirement, while real retirements keep their vocabulary
truths.evidence: config.mjs get __proto__ / get constructor / get toString each -> {"ok":false,"reason":"unknown-key","detail":["<key>"]} exit 1; get stakes __proto__ -> the same unknown-key refusal (no longer answering about one key of two), while get stakes alone still -> {"ok":true,"values":{"stakes":"shipped"},...} exit 0; check '__proto__=1' -> {"ok":false,"reason":"invalid","detail":[{"key":"__proto__","error":"unknown key"}]}, the fabricated 'retired in v2.0.0: undefined' is gone. Retirement vocabulary intact: check 'model.profile=1' still -> error 'retired in v2.0.0: use "stakes" instead ...' (the flagged assumption on lib/retired-keys.mjs holds).
